# Roles

Each user has one role, such as `manager` or `staff`.
You declare the roles in `spinup.toml`, and then you limit routes and pages to some roles.
The `auth` module must be on. See [Accounts and sign-in](../auth.md).

```toml
[auth]
roles = ["manager", "staff"]
admin_role = "manager"
default_role = "staff"
```

Then guard a resource or a page with one flag:

```sh
spinup g resource todo title:string --role manager
spinup g page reports --server --role manager
```

A role is a word that your app owns.
The kit, the generators, and the web app never test for a role name.

## Declare the roles

Edit the `[auth]` table of `spinup.toml`. Then run `spinup g roles`.
The command writes `api/internal/roles/roles.gen.go` with one constant for each role.
Run it again after each change to `[auth]`.

| Key | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `roles` | The list of role names. It has 1 to 16 unique names. | `["manager", "staff"]` |
| `admin_role` | The role of the first account in `first-user` mode. The kit also keeps at least one account with this role. | `manager` |
| `default_role` | The role of a self-service account and of an OIDC account. | `staff` |

Rules for a role name:

- Use lower-case letters, digits, and underscores. Start with a letter. Use 32 characters at most.
- Do not use a double underscore or a trailing underscore.
- Do not use `set`. The generated file already declares `Set`.
- Do not use two names that give the same Go constant.
- Put `admin_role` and `default_role` in `roles`.

If the table or a key is absent, the key has its default.

```console
$ spinup new todo --module example.com/todo --modules ci,auth --no-git --non-interactive
...
$ cd todo
$ cat api/internal/roles/roles.gen.go
// Code generated by spinup. DO NOT EDIT.

package roles

import "github.com/stopyellingatme/spinup/kit/auth"

const (
	// Manager is the "manager" role.
	Manager = "manager"
	// Staff is the "staff" role.
	Staff = "staff"
)

// Set is the role set of this app. Pass it to auth.WithRoles.
var Set = auth.Roles{Names: []string{Manager, Staff}, Admin: Manager, Default: Staff}
$ grep -E 'WithRoles|WithRegistration|WithCommand\("user"' api/cmd/api/main.go
		auth.WithRoles(roles.Set),
		auth.WithRegistration(auth.RegistrationMode(os.Getenv("AUTH_REGISTRATION"))),
		app.WithCommand("user", auth.UserCommand(authn)),
```

`main.go` passes `roles.Set` to the auth module with `auth.WithRoles`.
If it does not, the kit uses the default roles.
See [spinup g roles](../site/commands/generate-roles.md) for the command.

## Limit an API route to a role

Use `RequireRole` with the constants from the `roles` package.
It answers 401 without a user and 403 when the role of the user is not in the list.

```go
mux.Handle("DELETE /api/todos/{id}", authn.RequireRole(roles.Manager)(deleteTodo))
```

- A call with no name, or with a name that the app does not declare, panics at startup.
- The check runs after the rate limit and the cross-origin check.
- The 403 body is a problem detail: `Your role cannot use this endpoint. Try: sign in with an account that has a required role.`

To branch inside a handler, use `user.HasRole`.
It is true when the role of the user is one of the names. It is false for an empty list.

```go
user, _ := auth.UserFrom(r.Context())
if !user.HasRole(roles.Manager) {
	// Show the manager view only.
}
```

In tests, run a handler as a user with a role:

```go
h := authtest.AsRole(handler, 1, roles.Manager)
```

`authtest.AsUser(handler, user)` runs the handler as a user you build.
`authtest.As` gives a user with an empty role.

## Limit a resource to a role

Add `--role` to the generator. The handlers check the role after they check the user.

```sh
spinup g resource todo title:string --role manager
spinup g resource note body:text --role manager,staff
```

The flag guards all five operations of the resource.
The OpenAPI file gets a `403` response for each operation.
See [spinup g resource](../site/commands/generate-resource.md).

With the audit module, the history of the resource uses the same roles. To use other roles, add `--history-role manager,staff`. See [Audit trail](../audit.md).

Two behaviors need care:

- A caller with the wrong role who sends bad input gets 400 or 422 before 403. The caller learns only the shape of the schema.
- A role does not change the owner filter. A resource with `--role` and without `--shared` still shows each user only the rows of that user. To share rows between users, add `--shared`. The generator prints a note about this.

## Limit a web page to a role

Add `--role` and `--server` to the page generator. Only a server `load` can guard a page.

```sh
spinup g page reports --server --role manager
```

The generated page calls `requireRole(locals, url, ...roles)`.
You can call the same helper in any `load` function or form action:

```ts
import { requireRole } from '#lib/server/auth.js';
import type { PageServerLoad } from './$types';

export const load: PageServerLoad = ({ locals, url }) => {
	requireRole(locals, url, 'manager');
	return { title: 'Reports' };
};
```

Without a user, the helper redirects with status 303 to `/login?redirectTo=<path>`.
If the role is not in the list, it answers 403 with the text `Your role cannot open this page. Try: sign in with an account that has a required role.`
See [spinup g page](../site/commands/generate-page.md).

{: .note }
The navigation does not hide items by role. The Go guard and `requireRole` enforce access. `App.User` has the field `role`, so a page can hide a link for a better look.

## Give a user a role

The operator command `user` creates accounts and changes roles. It is the only way to change a role.
Run it from `api/`, or in the `api` container of a deployed app.

<!-- doctest: skip -->
```console
$ go run ./cmd/api user set-role --email bob@example.com --role staff
updated bob@example.com	staff
```

The cookie holds only a session token, and the session stores only the user ID. The API reads the role from the database on each request.
A role change applies to the next request, and the user does not sign in again.
The command also has `user list` and `user backfill`. See [the user command](../reference/app-commands.md#user) for all actions and for the run on a server.

{: .warning }
Before you rename or remove a role, run `user set-role` for each account that holds it. `user list` marks these accounts as `(undeclared)`. If you add the name back later, the old rows get power again, maybe with a new meaning.

## Empty and undeclared roles

Accounts from before the roles migration have an empty role.
An empty role reads as `default_role`, and it never gives administrator rights.
If `default_role` equals `admin_role`, an empty role matches no name.
New accounts always store a named role.

Run `user backfill` once. It writes `default_role` into the empty rows, so a later change of `default_role` does not move old accounts.
A stored role that the app no longer declares keeps its text, and `HasRole` is false for every declared role.

## Add roles to an existing app

`spinup upgrade` adds the role column and the role files to an app that has the `auth` module.
It creates `api/db/kit/00005_users_role.sql` and `api/internal/roles/roles.gen.go`.
It does not change `spinup.toml`.

1. Run `spinup upgrade --plan`. Read the notes. Then run `spinup upgrade --yes`.
2. If your app has its own file `00005_*.sql`, the plan prints a warning. Rename your migration to the next free number. Then run the upgrade again.
3. If `spinup.toml` has an `[auth]` table, run `spinup g roles`. The upgrade writes the default role file.
4. Check `api/cmd/api/main.go`. The upgrade merges this file in three ways. If the merge conflicts, add these lines by hand. Import `<module>/api/internal/roles` for `roles.Set`.

   ```go
   auth.WithRoles(roles.Set),
   auth.WithRegistration(auth.RegistrationMode(os.Getenv("AUTH_REGISTRATION"))),
   app.WithCommand("user", auth.UserCommand(authn)),
   ```

5. Run `spinup doctor`. The check `roles-drift` warns while a line is missing.
6. Run `spinup db migrate up` before you start the new binary. Without the role column, login fails with a 500. `spinup deploy` already migrates first.
7. Give the first administrator the admin role. Then run `user backfill`:

<!-- doctest: skip -->
```console
$ cd api
$ go run ./cmd/api user set-role --email ada@example.com --role manager
updated ada@example.com	manager
$ go run ./cmd/api user backfill
backfilled 12 accounts
```

If `main.go` does not register the `user` command, use SQL for the first administrator. Replace `manager` with your `admin_role`:

```sql
UPDATE users SET role = 'manager' WHERE email = lower('ada@example.com');
```

The migrator applies a pending migration with a lower version than the latest applied one.
So `00005` applies in an app that already applied `00004` or higher.
Until you run these steps, every existing account reads as `default_role`, and none is an administrator.

## The roles-drift check

`spinup doctor` runs the check `roles-drift`. It skips an app without the `auth` module. It warns when:

- `roles.gen.go` differs from `[auth]`. Run `spinup g roles`.
- `roles.gen.go` is missing. Run `spinup g roles`.
- `api/cmd/api/main.go` has no `auth.WithRoles(` call. Add the call by hand.

While the check warns, the app can run with a role set that differs from `spinup.toml`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spinup g roles` fails with `admin_role "x" must be in roles` | The `[auth]` table breaks a rule. | Correct `spinup.toml` and run the command again. |
| The API panics at startup in `RequireRole` | The call has no name, or a name that the app does not declare. | Use the constants from the `roles` package. |
| The build fails after you remove a role | A handler still uses the constant of the role. | Fix each use. The compiler finds them for you. |
| A user gets 403 on a page | The role of the user is not in the list. | Run `user set-role` for the account. |
